zh.title: 菲律賓空軍兩架SF-260教練機相撞致4死 國防部展開調查並停飛機隊
zh.summary: 菲律賓空軍兩架SF-260撞毀致4人殉職；國防部展開調查；空軍停飛同型機隊
body: 菲律賓國防部（DND）已針對菲律賓空軍（PAF）兩架SF-260教練機相撞墜毀事故展開調查。該起事故於2026年10月23日發生在八打雁省利帕市的費爾南多空軍基地（Fernando Air Base），導致機上4名飛行員全部殉職。國防部發布聲明表示，調查將秉持徹底與客觀原則，以釐清事實真相、確定事故原因，並找出需要採取糾正措施的漏洞，防止類似悲劇再次發生。

菲律賓國防部長吉爾伯託·特奧多羅（Gilberto Teodoro Jr.）指出，調查範圍將涵蓋飛行計畫、行政程序、飛行員訓練、維修保養以及指揮領導層面。調查人員將覈查兩架飛機的維修紀錄、留存可回收部件、審視涉事飛行員的過往表現，並在條件允許下進行毒物檢測。特奧多羅強調，空軍安全辦公室（Air Force Safety Office）將主導本次調查，且空軍對引進其他機構或夥伴國家的技術專家持開放態度。
根據報導，事故發生於當地時間2026年10月23日15時51分，當時兩架單引擎SF-260教練機正進行包括近距離編隊飛行在內的訓練任務。兩架飛機最終均墜毀於費爾南多空軍基地園區範圍內，未造成地面其他人員傷亡。事故發生後，菲律賓空軍已宣佈預防性停飛旗下所有SF-260教練機，並向殉職飛行員家屬表達深切哀悼與提供協助。
此起事故為菲律賓空軍近幾個月來發生的又一起SF-260墜機事件。2026年5月20日，一架SF-260教練機在執行長程航行訓練任務後，於班格特省圖巴（Tuba, Benguet）墜毀，造成一名女性飛行教官及其學員殉職。國防部長特奧多羅提醒公眾在調查進行期間切勿捕風捉影，強調過早下結論可能不公平地牽連無辜者或袒護責任人。

en.title: Philippines Probes SF-260 Trainer Aircraft Crash That Killed Four Pilots
en.summary: Philippine Air Force grounds SF-260 fleet as defense officials investigate fatal crash that killed four pilots.
body: The Department of National Defense (DND) of the Philippines has launched an investigation into a fatal midair collision involving two Philippine Air Force (PAF) SF-260 trainer aircraft. The accident occurred on October 23, 2026, at Fernando Air Base in Lipa City, Batangas, resulting in the deaths of all four pilots on board. In an official statement, the defense ministry affirmed its commitment to conducting a thorough and objective investigation to establish the facts, determine the underlying causes, and identify systemic gaps to prevent future occurrences.

Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. stated that the investigation will encompass flight planning, administrative procedures, pilot training, fleet maintenance, and command leadership. Investigators will trace the maintenance records of both single-engine aircraft, preserve salvaged components, examine the historical performance of the involved pilots, and perform toxicology testing if suitable samples remain available. The Air Force Safety Office is leading the probe, with Teodoro noting that the military remains open to seeking external technical assistance from partner nations if necessary.

The collision took place at 15:51 local time during a routine military training flight focused on close formation maneuvers. Both SF-260 aircraft impacted the ground within the perimeter of Fernando Air Base, and no additional casualties or ground damage were reported. Following the incident, the Philippine Air Force implemented a precautionary grounding of its entire operational SF-260 fleet while investigators evaluate potential contributing factors and safety procedures.

The crash marks the second fatal mishap involving the Philippine Air Force's SF-260 fleet in recent months. Earlier on May 20, 2026, an SF-260 trainer crashed in Tuba, Benguet, following a long-range navigation training mission, killing both an instructor pilot and her student. Defense officials cautioned against premature speculation while formal investigative processes are underway, emphasizing that official findings will be made public once verified facts are established.
